subject: Renewal: Proposal to double reserved GPUs and update pricing
messages:
From: Tom Liang <tom.liang@acmeai.com>
To: priya_natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodai.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Contract renewal coming up — capacity needs

Hi Priya,

Quick heads up — our contract with Redwood is up for renewal in January and usage has been consistently higher than our 16-GPU reserved pool. We ran a capacity projection and expect steady-state load that would benefit from doubling to 32 GPUs starting next quarter.

Two asks from our side: 1) a revised reserved pricing for 32 GPUs (we need predictable unit economics), and 2) a throughput guarantee or baseline so our service-level planning team can sign off. Any chance you can share a proposal this week?

Cc: sara.blake@acmeprocurement.com for procurement coordination.

Thanks,
Tom Liang
Head of Model Ops, Acme AI
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodai.com>
To: Tom Liang <tom.liang@acmeai.com>
Cc: Sara Blake <sara.blake@acmeprocurement.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 10:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Contract renewal coming up — capacity needs

Hi Tom — thanks for the heads up.

We can definitely support a move to 32 reserved GPUs for your production pool. Attached is a first-pass proposal that outlines: revised per-GPU reserved pricing, an end-to-end throughput baseline for your common 1.5k token workloads, and a suggested term structure (12 vs 24 months) with pro-rated ramp and a short trial for the additional capacity.

Highlights:
- Reserved price (32-GPU pool): $3.10 / GPU-hour (committed) — this is a blended rate for the doubled pool assuming a 12-month commitment.
- Throughput baseline: 1.9k tokens/sec aggregate (p99 tail under 300ms for streaming responses) for your 32-GPU partition; detailed numbers in throughput-sla-table.csv.
- Ramp credit: 10% credit on additional GPU hours for the first 30 days if we miss the p99 SLA.

I attached RDW-Proposal-Acme-32GPU-v2.pdf and the SLA table. Can you confirm the target start date and whether procurement prefers a 12- or 24-month term? Once you confirm, I can loop in finance for the formal amendment and a DocuSign packet.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Mobile: (415) 555-0192

Attachments: RDW-Proposal-Acme-32GPU-v2.pdf (proposal), throughput-sla-table.csv (SLA detail)
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodai.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodai.com>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwoodai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodai.com>
Date: Sat, 5 Dec 2026 09:41:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Contract renewal coming up — capacity needs — pricing check

Team — forwarding Acme's ask and the draft I sent. Key negotiation points they care about: unit economics (per-GPU reserved rate), p99 throughput SLA, and a clean billing ramp that doesn't spike their month 1 bill. They asked for a proposal this week.

Options I'm considering:
- Option A (12mo): $3.10 / GPU-hr for 32 GPUs, 30-day ramp credit (10%) if SLA missed.
- Option B (24mo): $2.85 / GPU-hr for 32 GPUs, 45-day ramp credit (15%), and a one-time onboarding credit of $10k.

Can finance run quick margin on both and confirm we can accept $2.85 on a 24mo? Dev, can ops confirm the p99 300ms promise for their 1.5k token profile and whether warm-up costs might change billing estimates?

Goal: send a revised offer that we can get signed by 12/15 so the new capacity can go live 1/15.

Thanks — Priya
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodai.com>
To: priya_natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodai.com>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwoodai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodai.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Dec 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Contract renewal coming up — pricing check

Priya — quick finance and ops read:

Finance: we can support Option B (24-month) at $2.85 / GPU-hr if Acme commits to a minimum throughput (utilization floor) of 55% across the pool to protect economics; otherwise we should stick to Option A. We should also limit the ramp credit cap to the equivalent of 48 hours of additional GPU consumption to avoid open-ended credits.

Ops (Dev): we can guarantee the p99 target for the specific 1.5k token workload as long as we reserve a dedicated KV cache allocation and maintain a minimum batch size policy that matches their call pattern. That is operationally fine for a dedicated 32-GPU partition starting 2027-01-15, but we need a one-week validation window post-deploy.

Proposed final terms to present to Acme:
- 24-month commitment: $2.85 / GPU-hour for 32 GPUs (RDW will provide one-time $10,000 onboarding credit).
- Utilization floor: 55% (monthly average) — if below, per-GPU rate adjusts +12% for shortfall months.
- SLA: p99 latency target as in SLA table; if we miss p99, customer receives a credit equal to up to 48 GPU-hours at the committed rate.
- Validation window: 7 days after cutover to confirm performance; ramp credits only executable after validation window.

If that looks good I can have legal sketch a short amendment and finance will prepare a DocuSign.

— Karthik
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodai.com>
To: Tom Liang <tom.liang@acmeai.com>, Sara Blake <sara.blake@acmeprocurement.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodai.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodai.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Updated offer: 32-GPU reserved pool (24-month preferred)

Tom / Sara — thanks for the quick sync earlier. Per internal review, here's the updated offer we'd like you to consider:

Summary (preferred): 24-month commitment for a dedicated 32-GPU reserved pool
- Committed rate: $2.85 / GPU-hour (applies to all 32 GPUs while committed)
- One-time onboarding credit: $10,000 applied to your first invoice
- Utilization floor: 55% monthly average (see note below)
- SLA: p99 latency target (detailed in attached throughput-sla-table.csv). If we miss p99 after the 7-day validation window, Acme receives a credit up to 48 GPU-hours at the committed rate.
- Start date target: 2027-01-15; validation window: 7 calendar days following cutover.

Notes:
- If you prefer a 12-month term we can do $3.10 / GPU-hour with the same SLA but reduced onboarding credit (no $10k).
- Utilization floor exists to keep the reserved economics predictable; we can include a quarterly review cadence to revisit utilization assumptions.

Next steps: I uploaded the amendment and a DocuSign packet here: https://docusign.example.com/ABC123. Please review and signal preferred term (24 vs 12 months) and desired start date.

Regards,
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Office: (415) 555-0100

Attachments: RDW-Proposal-Acme-32GPU-v2.pdf, throughput-sla-table.csv
From: Sara Blake <sara.blake@acmeprocurement.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodai.com>
Cc: Tom Liang <tom.liang@acmeai.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodai.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Dec 2026 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Updated offer: 32-GPU reserved pool (24-month preferred)

Priya — apologies for the slow reply, procurement needed to align with finance. Acme is happy to move forward on the 24-month commitment at $2.85 / GPU-hour with the $10k onboarding credit. Two small requests before we sign:

1) Can the start date be 2027-01-22 instead of 01-15? That gives our infra team an extra week to complete the change window.
2) For the first invoice, can you confirm you will pro-rate the additional 16 GPUs for the partial month and show the credit line separately so our accounting team can map it to our P&L?

If you can confirm those two points in writing we will execute the DocuSign packet today. Thanks to Karthik for working through the terms with us.

Best,
Sara Blake
Senior Procurement Manager, Acme AI
